acceptanceCriteria: Retain a reproducible instrumented/uninstrumented comparison and identify why the measured allocation exceeds the ceiling; distinguish test accounting from product allocation behavior.
Keep the intended ordinary allocation budget and meaningful functional race coverage; do not silently raise the ceiling or skip the entire capacity proof.
After separately authorized repair, retain independent review, exact checks and hosted CI evidence; keep the original broader GH399 qualification limits explicit.
body:
Confirmed hosted failure at PR418 head d99b49cf60ca570a36f18346d3a0fc11fff44e94, Linux/amd64 Go1.27.1 with go test -json -p 1 -count=1 -race -timeout 50m. Run36840028834 job110297085688 failed TestIndexedCorpusCapacityQualification/DCP-V1-040_synthetic_25000_claims_5000_symbols at internal/corpusindex/index_test.go:200 after116.99s: synthetic open/query exceeded 1GiB allocation ceiling. The counter brackets indexed Open/Query plus native ParseArtifact/Query and receipt encoding; no exact failing byte total was printed. Prior ordinary local Darwin/arm64 focused proof at8b6ad1ce passed and logged total allocation566586664. Race instrumentation, platform differences and unrelated global allocation activity are hypotheses, not confirmed root cause. Existing analyzer allocation tests in the same hosted log explicitly distinguish race instrumentation. Raw/normalized evidence: /tmp/corvint-parallel-dispatch/corpus90-hosted-shard1.raw.log and corpus90-hosted-shard1.log. Root is running the isolated unchanged test with -race for diagnosis only. Core installedbuild163, Tasksbuild202. Dedup searches1GiB/allocation ceiling/synthetic found no equivalent; V1-0584 concerns separate local proof gaps. Public proof repair cycle1 and documentation CI repaircycle2 are exhausted; no third code repair or limit relaxation is authorized by this record.

Bounded local reproduction: unchanged d99b49cf, Go1.27.1 Darwin/arm64, isolated go test -count=1 -race -timeout30m -run ^TestIndexedCorpusCapacityQualification$ -v ./internal/corpusindex reproduced the same ceiling failure (test83.64s, supervised wall87.63s, exit1). This weakens Linux-only and cross-test contamination explanations; instrumentation-associated allocation remains the strongest hypothesis, not an exact byte-accounting explanation. Prior ordinary source test output is retained, not relabelled. Source was not edited, ceiling unchanged, and owned process group retired. Logs/result: corpus90-capacity-race-repro.log and corpus90-capacity-race-repro-result.json in /tmp/corvint-parallel-dispatch. Existing analogous allocation guards: internal/analyzercap/runtime_admission_test.go:1136-1160 with race_enabled_test.go/race_disabled_test.go. Any repair must preserve ordinary budget proof and functional instrumented checks.

Controlled paired ordinary run on the SAME d99b49cf source and Darwin/arm64 Go1.27.1 passed with only -race removed: total_alloc=767732232 bytes, retained_heap=144510152, corpus_bytes=29811203, index_bytes=34750940, test17.65s (supervised19.568s), exit0. Both owned process groups retired. This demonstrates the ceiling failure is instrumented-mode-dependent on this host; the exact extra allocation mechanism and ordinary Linux allocation remain NOT_OBSERVED. Raw paired logs/results retained in corpus90-capacity-{race,ordinary}-repro*.

2026-10-01 additional observation (PR438 declared-read-scope re-derivation, golang:1.27.1 linux/arm64 container, no -race): with three packages running in parallel (xargs -P3), TestIndexedCorpusCapacityQualification/DCP-V1-040_synthetic_25000_claims_5000_symbols failed at index_test.go:202 'synthetic open/query exceeded 1GiB allocation ceiling' after 19.6s in the Landlock-confined run while the unconfined parallel run passed; two serial reruns passed in both modes (about 19s each). An earlier derivation pass under parallel load instead missed this test's time budget. So the ceiling is also sensitive to concurrent host load, not only race instrumentation.
title: Corpus capacity allocation ceiling fails in race-instrumented CI
